blocks.text: Re: Executive messaging engagement
Dear Jennifer:

This letter sets out the basis on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC ("Ashcombe") will work with {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} (the "Company") on the messaging its executive team uses with investors, analysts, employees and the press. It follows our conversations with you over recent weeks, and we have tried to record them faithfully. Where it departs from your understanding, please tell us before you sign, and we will correct it.
The work we will undertake

Our task is to help the Company's senior leadership describe the business, its performance and its priorities in terms that hold steady from one audience to the next. By the close of the engagement, we expect the executive team to have a core narrative, supporting messages for each of its principal audiences, and talking points and question-and-answer material that its spokespeople have rehearsed.

We propose to proceed in three stages. We will first review the Company's recent public statements, investor materials and internal communications, and speak with those members of the leadership team you identify. We will then draft the narrative and its supporting messages for discussion with you and, once these are settled, prepare and rehearse the materials the spokespeople will use.

We will give particular attention to the agreement between what the Company tells investors and what it tells its own employees, since the two are often read side by side. The narrative will be written so that the finance function can stand behind every figure on which it relies.

Each draft will pass through your review before it is shared more widely within the Company, and nothing we prepare will be used externally without the Company's written approval. The engagement does not extend to legal review of disclosures, the preparation of financial information, or the purchase of media. Where a draft touches on a matter that the Company's counsel or auditors should see, we will identify it so that their review can take place first.
Your team at Ashcombe

I will retain overall responsibility for the engagement and will read the principal materials before they reach you. Michael Morris, a Partner of the firm, will lead the work from day to day and will be your first call on timing and priorities.

John Macias, an Associate, will prepare first drafts of the narrative, statements and question-and-answer material. Amy Carter, a Communications Associate, will develop the investor-facing messages and talking points, and will check each claim against the source that supports it.

We understand that you will act as the Company's principal contact for the engagement. Unless you direct otherwise, we will route drafts, questions and requests for approval through you. Should the needs of the work change, we may draw on other members of the firm, and we will tell you before any change is made to the team named here.
How we will work together

We propose to keep you informed through a single email thread for status and approvals, with working sessions whenever a draft is ready for discussion. We will agree the schedule of leadership interviews with you at the outset, and we will ask for the documents we need to review in a single request at the same time, so that your team is not asked for material piece by piece.
Commencement and fee

The engagement will commence on {{fact:f:E-2023-001.start}}, and we anticipate that it will run for approximately five months. Should the Company's own calendar call for a different pace, we will agree any change with you in writing.

For the services described in this letter, the Company will pay Ashcombe a fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2023-001.fee}}. The fee covers the time of the team named above, however many rounds of drafting the agreed scope requires.
Invoicing and payment

We will invoice the fee in equal monthly installments across the term of the engagement, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as travel to rehearsal sessions, will be billed at cost, and we will ask for your approval before incurring any expense of significance.
Term and termination

This letter takes effect when signed by both parties and continues until the work described above is complete. Either party may end the engagement at any time by written notice to the other. In that event, the Company will pay the portion of the fee attributable to work performed up to the date of notice, together with any approved expenses already incurred.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company shares with us, use it only for the purposes of this engagement, and disclose it within Ashcombe only to those working on it. Some of that information may be material, and our team will observe the Company's policies on trading and disclosure as they apply to outside advisers. These obligations continue after the engagement ends, and at its close we will return or destroy the Company's documents on request, keeping only such copies as we are required to retain for our own records.
Limitation of liability

Our advice concerns communications and is not legal, accounting or investment advice; the Company retains sole responsibility for the content and accuracy of any statement it makes. To the fullest extent the law permits, Ashcombe's total liability arising from this engagement will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss.
Governing law

This letter, and any dispute that arises under it, will be construed under the laws of the state of Ashcombe's organization, without giving effect to principles of conflict of laws. Together with any variation in writing signed on behalf of both parties, it is the complete statement of our agreement on this engagement.
Acceptance

We are glad to be working with you and your colleagues, and we look forward to the first conversations with the leadership team. If these terms reflect your understanding, please sign where indicated below and return a copy to me. Once we have it, Michael will be in touch to arrange the kickoff with your team.
Signed for Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC and, in acceptance of these terms, on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}:
Kickoff: Executive Messaging for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}

To: Michael Morris, Amy Carter, Julie Bailey
From: John Macias
Re: Objectives, who does what, and the first two weeks
What we are here to do

{{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} has asked us to help its executive team tell one consistent story about the business. The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2023-001.start}} and runs about five months. Jennifer Herrera, VP Finance, is our client lead. She sees every draft before it goes to the wider leadership team. The engagement letter is signed, so the scope is settled.

By the end, the leadership team should have three things. The first is a core narrative. The second is a set of messages for each audience that matters to them: investors, analysts, employees and the press. The third is talking points and Q&A they have practiced out loud. Everything below serves one of those three.
How the work splits

items: Discovery. Read the public statements, investor materials and internal all-hands decks from the past year, and run the leadership interviews. Lead: John Macias, with Michael Morris in the interviews.
Core narrative. Turn what we hear into a draft narrative and its supporting messages. Lead: John Macias. Michael reviews before anything goes to Jennifer.

Investor messages and talking points. Build the investor-facing messages and check every claim against a source the company can stand behind. Lead: Amy Carter, working with Jennifer on anything that touches the numbers.
Q&A and rehearsal. Draft the hard questions and the answers, then rehearse with the spokespeople. John drafts. Amy takes the finance questions.
Consistency and style. Read each draft against house style and against the approved narrative, so the pieces agree with each other. Lead: Julie Bailey.

blocks.text: Ground rules

Status and approvals go through one email thread with Jennifer. Drafts live in the shared folder, with a version number in each file name. Michael copies the whole team when a decision lands, so nobody works from an old version.

Every figure in the claims log needs a source. If a figure has none, it stays out of the draft until Jennifer confirms it. Legal review of disclosures is not part of our scope. Where a draft touches something the company's counsel should see, we flag it to Jennifer and wait.
The first two weeks
Everything starts with the source documents. Jennifer has offered to send them as soon as we ask, and the interviews depend on them. So the order matters.
I will send Jennifer the document request on Monday. When she confirms which members of the leadership team we should speak with, Michael and I will propose interview slots.

Amy, the claims log will save us rounds of edits later. Could you start it from the investor materials as they arrive? Julie, we will be sharing a lot of drafts with one client contact. Could you set up the shared folder and a short style sheet for this account?
Michael, the interviews will go better if the leadership team knows why we are asking. Could you send Jennifer a few lines she can pass on to them?
If the split looks wrong to anyone, tell me and I will take another pass. Otherwise, the document request goes to Jennifer on Monday, and I will copy all of you when it does.
Good morning Jennifer,
I am starting this thread so that status and approvals on the executive messaging work for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} sit in one place. Amy and Michael are copied, and we will all reply here.

Here is where things stand. We have finished reading the materials your team sent, including the investor presentation and the all-hands slides. All but one of the leadership interviews are done, and the notes are written up. The interviews were candid and useful. A few themes came up more than once, and they will shape the first draft. Amy has also started the claims log, which lists each figure and statement the messages will rely on, with its source.

Two things from your side would keep us on plan. The remaining interview is not yet on the calendar, so could you suggest a time in the next week or so? The claims log will also need a finance check, so could you let us know whether you will review it yourself or pass it to someone on your team?
Once that last interview is done, I will send you the first draft of the core narrative.
Regards,
Hi Jennifer,

I want to add one point to John's note, because the first draft of the narrative will lean on the growth priorities your leadership team described in the interviews, and some of that material is forward-looking in a way your counsel may want to see before it circulates any further inside {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}.

With that in mind, there are two things I would ask you to decide when you have a moment:
1. Whether counsel should review the draft narrative at the first round, alongside you, or only once you and we have settled the wording between us.
2. Whether you would like to walk through the first draft with us on a call, with the text in front of everyone, or to receive it by email and send your comments back in writing.
Either answer works for the timing we agreed, and John will plan the next draft around whichever you choose.
Sincerely,
Good morning Jennifer,
Following Michael's note, it may help to see which parts of the draft would go to counsel. So far there are three passages.

items: The paragraph on growth priorities for the coming years, which is forward-looking.
The description of margin improvement, which uses figures from the interviews that we have not yet matched to a published source.
A sentence on new markets, which refers to plans that have not been announced.

blocks.text: The rest of the draft draws on material that {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} has already put out publicly.

If counsel does review at the first round, I can send just those three passages, each with a short note on where it came from. That should keep their read short. I will hold the draft until we hear which you prefer.
Regards,
Hi Jennifer,

John's list covers the passages I had in mind, and since none of them needs to hold up the rest of the draft, I suggest we send the three marked passages to counsel now and carry on with the remainder of the narrative at the same time, so that counsel's comments and yours reach us at about the same point.

To do that we need two things from you:
1. The name and email address of the person on counsel's side who should receive the passages, or a line confirming that you would rather forward them yourself.
2. An hour early next week for a walkthrough of the full draft, ideally with whoever at {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} will review the finance language, so that Amy can take their questions on the claims log in the same sitting.
If it is easier to settle both by phone, I am at my desk until about six this evening and can call you.
Sincerely,
